note: Threat-evidence backfill: real conformance test at crates/chio-conformance/tests/threats/wasm_guard_resource_exhaustion.rs imports chio_wasm_guards::runtime::wasmtime_backend::WasmtimeBackend directly and drives the SAME production runtime-execution surface used by the kernel host pipeline. The Risk Register R3 entry that previously listed this row as BLOCKED-BY-ARCHITECTURE was scoped to wasm-guard SDK v4 (multi-tenant arena work, DEFERRED-FOLLOW-UP); the production fuel-budget and module-size enforcement that THIS threat row targets is in tree today and is exercised here. Two deny-asserting arms cover the sub-vectors: (1) fuel-budget overrun -- an attacker-controlled guard module with an infinite loop traps under a 5_000_000-fuel cap with WasmGuardError::FuelExhausted or fuel-related Trap; (2) module-size cap -- a blob above the configured DEFAULT_MAX_MODULE_SIZE is rejected at WasmtimeBackend::load_module with WasmGuardError::ModuleTooLarge { size, limit }. A benign round-trip arm guards against over-rejection. The chio-wasm-guards/tests/escape/ harness pins are retained as a supplementary regression net. Header documents the revert-to-prove-it-fails recipe (relax the max_module_size guard inside WasmtimeBackend::load_module).
